name: Heartswood
summary: In the years since the Third War, Heartswood draws warlocks toward an old night elf tragedy. Takar the Seer sends them into Ashenvale for Gakin the Darkbinder, who needs the wood to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind.

sections.title: A Monument to Tragic Love
sections.body: Takar the Seer says Heartswood grew where the night elf lovers Anathera and Latherion fell during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Their last breaths and devotion nourished the tree. To mortal eyes, it marks a tragic love; to practitioners of the dark arts, its concentrated emotion is potent magical fuel.

sections.title: Baiting the Succubus
sections.body: Succubi feed on mortal passion, desire, and torment. Takar knows ordinary temptations cannot match an artifact filled with thousands of years of devotion. A piece of Heartswood gives Gakin the Darkbinder the catalyst he needs to draw a cunning demon through the Nether and into a summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

sections.title: The Ruins of Ordil'Aran
sections.body: The Heartswood tree grows among the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. Wild beasts, hostile lands, and Dark Strand cultists who have occupied the elven ruins stand in the way. Once recovered, the wood must cross the sea to the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, where the ritual of subjugation begins.

faq.q: Why do warlocks need Heartswood to summon a succubus?
faq.answer: Succubi are drawn to passion, desire, and strong emotional bonds. Heartswood grew where two devoted night elf lovers died together ten thousand years ago, and their lingering passion fills the wood. That makes it ideal bait to draw a succubus through the Nether.

faq.q: Where does the Heartswood tree grow?
faq.answer: The Heartswood tree grows in the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, in northwestern Ashenvale, not far south of Darkshore. Sinister cultists have taken control of the area.

Anathera and Latherion were night elves who fought side by side during the War of the Ancients. They fell together on the battlefield, and Heartswood grew where they drew their last breaths, marking their enduring love.

Takar the Seer is a human seer allied with Stormwind's warlocks. He lives as a hermit in the southern Barrens near Camp Taurajo, using his sight to look into the past and find forgotten relics for Gakin the Darkbinder.

faq.q: How does an Alliance warlock travel safely to Ashenvale from the Barrens?
faq.answer: Alliance travelers crossing the Barrens must avoid the Horde outpost at the Mor'shan Rampart, where guards watch closely. Warlocks can slip through an unguarded breach just east of the main gate, take the high road through Stonetalon, or swim the border river.

faq.q: What happens after Gakin receives the Heartswood?
aliases: what does gakin do with heartswood
faq.answer: Gakin uses the wood to prepare a ritual in the catacombs beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind. He draws a summoning circle to pull a succubus from the Twisting Nether, then tasks the warlock with defeating and subjugating her.

angles.text: As a warlock, you need Heartswood to summon and enslave a succubus, whose powers can turn your enemies' minds against them on the battlefield.
As an Alliance spellcaster, you cross contested wilderness and face hostile Horde outposts among ancient night elf ruins in Kalimdor.
As a human, you may rely on far-flung scouts like Takar the Seer to find relics from old Kalimdor, beyond what human arcanists have recorded.
